- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices during strong negative sentiment (sentiment < 0.2) — adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid underreaction.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment is positive.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strong.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was high 3–5 days prior, forecast should be 2–3% higher than baseline.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in trend — reduce first 5–7 days if sentiment is rising.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is rising but price is flat, don’t extrapolate upward; wait for confirmation.
